title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typescript page, numbered 33, is not Grothendieck's motivic material. It reads like a Bourbaki-style or textbook rédaction on analytic functions of one or several variables over K = R or C, probably misfiled in cote 15. It cites 'chap. I, §2, th. 1', which says a continuous function whose square is z is holomorphic.

The page finishes a counterexample and then strengthens the identity principle (analytic continuation from A to A∪B).

(1) Counterexample. Take two open sectors in C*. A is the set of z with argument θ ∈ (−π, π) satisfying −2π/3 < θ < 2π/3. B is the set of z with argument θ' ∈ (0, 2π) satisfying π/3 < θ' < 5π/3. Their intersection A∩B has two components, H (−2π/3 < θ < −π/3) and H' (π/3 < θ < 2π/3). The branches f = √|z| e^{iθ/2} on A and g = √|z| e^{i(θ'−2π)/2} on B are holomorphic square roots of z. On H we have θ' = θ + 2π, so f = g. On H' we have θ' = θ, so f = −g. So f and g agree on a nonempty open subset of A∩B but do not glue to a function on A∪B. Hence connectedness of A∩B is needed in the gluing / analytic continuation statement.

(2) Remarks weakening the hypothesis 'f = g on a nonempty open U ⊂ A∩B'. Write h = f − g.
- Over C it suffices that h vanish on U∩V, where V is a real affine subspace {Im z_k = β_k, 1 ≤ k ≤ p}. At a ∈ U∩V each complex partial derivative ∂/∂z_k of h equals the real partial derivative in the direction Re z_k, which is tangent to V. So all Taylor coefficients of h at a vanish, and h ≡ 0 near a.
- In one variable (over R or C) it suffices that h vanish on a set M whose intersection with some compact neighbourhood U ⊂ A∩B is infinite. Compactness gives an accumulation point b ∈ U of zeros, and the isolated-zeros principle gives h ≡ 0 near b. Then one concludes as before, using connectedness.

This is the standard uniqueness theorem for analytic functions.
errors: In the last line of part 1 the second component should be H', not H ('et dans H', θ' = θ, d'où f(z) = −g(z)'). The computation itself is correct: f = g on H and f = −g on H'.

In the second remark 'p = 1' must mean dimension one (functions of one variable), since the isolated-zeros argument only works in one variable. This clashes with the earlier use of p as the number of equations defining V; it is a notational ambiguity in the typescript.
Both remarks implicitly need A∩B connected (or the conclusion is only on the component containing the point) to 'conclude as before'. The text leaves this implicit.

ideas.what: Gluing branches of √z on two sectors whose intersection is disconnected, to show that connectedness of A∩B is necessary for analytic continuation
ideas.modern_name: Failure of analytic continuation / monodromy of √z; identity theorem needs connected intersection
ideas.where_published: Standard in textbooks (e.g. Cartan's Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques)

ideas.what: Identity principle from vanishing on U ∩ {Im z_k = β_k}: complex derivatives equal real directional derivatives
ideas.modern_name: Identity theorem on (partly) real slices; uniqueness from totally real subsets

ideas.what: One-variable identity principle from infinitely many zeros in a compact subset

deep.surprise_reason: Routine textbook complex analysis: a √z counterexample and the identity theorem. It is apparently a stray page of a course or Bourbaki draft misfiled among the motivic Galois theory notes. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 'et dans H , θ'=θ' — the typescript itself has H here, but the sense requires H'.
Handwritten marginal number '63' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
